item.title: Patterns of Progression on Posttreatment Imaging During [<sup>177</sup>Lu]Lu-PSMA Radiopharmaceutical Therapy.
item.author: Yadav S, Khan S, Moradi Tuchayi A, Moradpour M, Nwihim S, de Kouchkovsky I, Flavell RR, Aggarwal RR, Emmett L, Hope TA.
item.description:
We characterized patterns of treatment response and progression during [ 177 Lu]Lu-PSMA radiopharmaceutical therapy (RPT) using serial posttreatment SPECT/CT and prostate-specific membrane antigen (PSMA) PET imaging and evaluated cycle-by-cycle prostate-specific antigen (PSA)-imaging concordance. Methods: We retrospectively analyzed 361 patients from 2 academic centers who received at least 2 cycles of [ 177 Lu]Lu-PSMA RPT between May 2017 and March 2025. Posttreatment SPECT/CT scans were qualitatively evaluated to determine the site and pattern of response and progression, including PSMA low-avidity and PSMA-negative disease. Progression was defined by the appearance of new lesions or at least a 2-fold growth in preexisting lesions on SPECT/CT. item.title: Impact of PSMA PET/CT Staging on Long-Term Outcomes in Patients with Clinically Localized Prostate Cancer: Results of a Large Single-Center Cohort.
item.author: Esmaeilzadeh Asl S, Hoberück S, Sonnenfeld A, Stange T, Böhme H, Klimova A, Rentsch A, Hölscher T, Boehm K, Thomas C, Miederer M.
item.description:
Prostate-specific membrane antigen (PSMA) PET/CT has become the gold standard for staging and restaging prostate cancer, with superior diagnostic accuracy over conventional imaging and established prognostic value. However, there are limited data on whether PSMA PET/CT-improved staging accuracy is associated with improved long-term patient outcomes. This study analyzes the association between PSMA PET/CT at primary staging and overall survival (OS), biochemical recurrence (BCR), and cancer-specific survival (CSS) in a large university hospital cohort at a center where PSMA PET/CT has been clinically available for over 13 y. Methods: This retrospective single-center study included all 11,146 patients with prostate cancer diagnosed between 2013 and 2023. item.title: Role of [<sup>18</sup>F]F-Fluciclovine PET/CT in Patients with Biochemical Recurrence of Prostate Cancer and Negative PSMA PET Results: A Single-Center Study.
item.author: Szidonya L, Obrzut S, Lim JY, Latour E, Choudhary G, Hung A, Mallak N.
item.description:
Our purpose was to evaluate whether [ 18 F]F-fluciclovine PET/CT detects sites of disease in patients with biochemical recurrence (BCR) of prostate cancer and negative findings on prostate-specific membrane antigen (PSMA) PET and to assess its impact on intended management. Methods: In this prospective single-arm study (NCT05722925), 50 patients with BCR (prostate-specific antigen [PSA] ≥ 0.2 ng/mL) and negative findings on PSMA PET underwent [ 18 F]F-fluciclovine PET/CT within 30 d of the previous imaging. Detection rate, distribution of disease, PSA-stratified analysis, management impact, and correct localization rate were assessed using descriptive statistics and exact CI. item.author: Borm FJ, Smit J, Gerards NR, Wiegers SE, van der Noort V, Wang Y, Cohen D, Monkhorst K, Grootendorst DJ, Leung D, Boellaard R, Smit EF, de Langen AJ.
item.description:
Programmed death ligand 1 (PD-L1) immunohistochemistry, the current standard biomarker for predicting response to programmed death protein 1/PD-L1 checkpoint inhibitors in non-small cell lung cancer, has moderate predictive value among others because of tumor heterogeneity and limited biopsy representation, whereas PD-L1 PET/CT using 18 F-BMS-986192 enables noninvasive, whole-tumor assessment of PD-L1 expression and heterogeneity, potentially improving prediction of response to immunotherapy. item.title: Botulinum Toxin Plus Transdermal Scopolamine Reduces Salivary Gland Uptake in Patients Undergoing Tandem Radiopharmaceutical Therapy with [<sup>225</sup>Ac]Ac- and [<sup>177</sup>Lu]Lu-PSMA Radioligands.
item.author: Mueller J, Zhao T, Jakobsson V, Shiyam Sundar LK, Fan X, Eismant A, Zhang J, Baum RP.
item.description:
Prostate-specific membrane antigen (PSMA)-targeted radiopharmaceutical therapy (RPT) has shown remarkable efficacy in advanced metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. However, salivary gland toxicity is a major dose-limiting adverse effect, particularly with α-emitting radionuclides such as 225 Ac. Although tandem therapy with combined [ 225 Ac]Ac- and [ 177 Lu]Lu-labeled PSMA-targeted RPT in a single low-activity cycle may address certain challenges, effective salivary gland protection remains crucial. In this study, we explored the use of botulinum toxin (BTX) type A (incobotulinumtoxinA) plus transdermal scopolamine as a protective strategy to mitigate salivary gland uptake of PSMA radioligands. item.title: Predicting [<sup>90</sup>Y]Y-FAPI-46 Tumor Absorbed Dose from Single-Time-Point [<sup>68</sup>Ga]Ga-FAPI-46 PET/CT Imaging.
item.author: Watanabe M, Jentzen W, Herrmann K, Kersting D, Fragoso Costa P.
item.description:
Radiolabeled fibroblast activation protein (FAP)-targeting peptides, such as 90 Y-FAPI-46, have increasingly been used to treat various tumor entities, with preliminary reports indicating therapeutic responses with acceptable toxicity profiles. Dosimetry can be used to maximize antitumor capability and minimize side effects. The aim of this study was to investigate whether 90 Y-FAPI-46 tumor dosimetry can be predicted by diagnostic 68 Ga-FAPI-46 PET/CT data. Methods: Fourteen patients with 24 lesions underwent a single-time-point 68 Ga-FAPI-46 PET/CT scan and 3 90 Y-FAPI-46 PET/CT scans for dosimetry within a 3-mo interval.
